title: A Orchard for the Compass
premise: In 1938, in a mountain town where an old observatory keeps the region's official time, apprentice clockmaker Jude Nakamura is summoned to repair the master clock and discovers its case hides a ledger of names — townsfolk who sheltered immigrants and dissidents for decades, including her own late mother. When the army requisitions the town and seizes every record it can find, Jude realizes the ledger's missing pages are the only proof that Captain Aldric Voss, now declared an enemy officer, was once the boy her family swore to protect. Torn between loyalty to her found family at the observatory and the truth that could save or doom them all, Jude races to restore both the clock and the ledger before the army's audit. In the end she chooses truth over silence: she testifies, the ledger is entered into the record, Voss is spared but exiled, and Jude becomes the observatory's keeper — an orchard planted from seeds hidden in the clock case blooming as the final image.
about_author: Jude Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former horologist's assistant who spent a decade restoring tower clocks across Europe before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for meticulous period detail and quiet characters who make loud moral choices.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Jude Nakamura arrives at the hilltop observatory to repair the master clock, navigating the wary kindness of head keeper Marta Ilves and the other apprentices who have become her found family. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: cautious belonging — she has learned which silences keep people safe, and this place taught her them.

chapters.title: What the Case Conceals
chapters.summary: Opening the clock's housing, Jude finds a hidden compartment containing a leather ledger of names, dates, and small pressed flowers — including her mother's handwriting beside her own childhood name. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: vertigo; the safe silences of five years crack open.

chapters.title: Marta's Long Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marta explains the ledger: forty years of the observatory recording who was sheltered, fed, hidden. She makes Jude swear to tell no one until the clock runs again. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: trust extended as a burden, not a gift.

chapters.title: A Boy Called Aldric
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: young Jude remembers the summer a frightened boy named Aldric Voss hid in the clock room, and the promise she made — that if he ever needed it, the ledger would speak for him. POV: Jude (memory). Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Army lorries roll into town; officers announce the observatory and all civic records are requisitioned for an audit of 'foreign elements.' The apprentices watch soldiers carry archive boxes down the hill. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: helplessness hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Inventorying what remains, Jude discovers the ledger's final section — including Voss's entry — has been torn out. Someone got there first. Suspicion falls within the family itself. POV: fellow apprentice Tomas. Emotional beat: betrayal's cold draft inside a warm house.

chapters.title: Officer Brandt's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Auditor Officer Brandt interviews Jude, polite and precise, probing her name, her mother, her loyalties. She performs the silence she was taught. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: terror wearing the mask of competence.

chapters.title: The Clock That Lies
chapters.summary: Jude realizes the master clock has been deliberately slowed by someone inside — minutes shaved daily to falsify the official timestamps on the seized records. The sabotage is protection, and treason. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: admiration tangled with fear.

chapters.title: Orchard Rows
chapters.summary: In the observatory's neglected orchard, Marta reveals the pressed flowers in the ledger match trees planted for each person saved. Jude finds one sapling with no ledger page — Voss's tree, cut down years ago. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: grief made botanical; love that leaves physical evidence.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Pendulum Glass
chapters.summary: Cleaning the pendulum case, Jude finds a letter in Voss's adult hand, mailed before the war closed borders: he is coming back, he needs his page, he trusts her promise. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the past arriving with a deadline.

chapters.title: Brandt Closes the Net
chapters.summary: The audit accelerates; a clerk who once appears in the ledger is arrested in the square. Marta burns nothing and confesses nothing, but begins teaching Jude which questions to answer slowly. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: defiance as inheritance.

chapters.title: Tomas's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tomas admits he removed the pages — not to betray anyone, but to sell them to Brandt in exchange for his brother's release. He begs Jude's silence. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: shame meeting compassion; loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Midnight Adjustment
chapters.summary: Jude must decide whether to correct the sabotaged clock — restoring true time and exposing the falsified records, or preserving the lie that shields dozens of names. She restores it, minute by minute, alone at night. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: choosing truth even when it cuts her own family.

chapters.title: The Man at the Treeline
chapters.summary: Aldric Voss appears at the orchard fence at dusk, gaunt, in civilian clothes, asking only for his page and one hour of shelter. Jude must hide him under the same roof as the army's auditors. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: a peacetime promise arriving in wartime.

chapters.title: One Hour in the Clock Room
chapters.summary: Voss and Jude keep vigil among the gears while Brandt dines downstairs. They reconstruct his torn page from memory, pressed flowers, and the stump of his felled tree. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: fragile rekindled trust; two people keeping time together.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Tomas, desperate and watched, tips off Brandt. Soldiers search the observatory at dawn. Marta stalls them with ceremony and procedure while Jude moves Voss through the orchard's old root cellar. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: guilt detonating; the cost of half-loyalties.

chapters.title: The Arrest of Marta Ilves
chapters.summary: The search fails to find Voss, so Brandt arrests Marta instead, charging her with falsifying civic time and harboring 'undocumented persons.' The found family fractures under interrogation schedules. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: rage and responsibility — her restored clock gave Brandt his evidence.

chapters.title: Ledger and Testimony
chapters.summary: Jude makes her choice: she delivers the reconstructed page and the original ledger to the tribunal, testifying to forty years of rescues, naming names, including her mother's and her own. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the climax — silence finally broken, at maximum personal risk.

chapters.title: What Truth Buys
chapters.summary: The testimony forces Brandt's superiors to intervene: the audit is discredited as overreach, Marta is released, Tomas's brother freed, and Tomas himself spared but stripped of his post. Voss is cleared yet ordered deported as a former enemy national. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: victory with amputations.

chapters.title: Departure Time
chapters.summary: At the station, Jude gives Voss his ledger page and a cutting grafted from his tree's surviving rootstock. They keep the promise precisely: neither asks the other to stay. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: love expressed as letting go, on schedule.

chapters.title: Setting the Rate
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Jude regulates the master clock to perfect time and formally signs the observatory's register as acting keeper, Marta watching. The apprentices rebuild the orchard rows, one sapling per name. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: identity claimed — no longer apprentice, no longer silent.

chapters.title: An Orchard for the Compass
chapters.summary: Years on, a letter arrives bearing no return address, only a pressed blossom from a tree grown in another country. Jude plants a new row and enters a fresh name in the continuing ledger. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: resolution — truth and loyalty reconciled as a living, growing thing.
